## Where it comes from

A plain sign whose pictorial origin the lists leave unsettled —
what is certain is its sound: *ša*, carried over from Sumerian
use into Akkadian, where it hit the jackpot. Akkadian's genitive
particle and relative pronoun is the word *ša*, so this one sign
writes "which," "who," and "of" across the entire corpus — the
fifth most frequent syllable in the Old Babylonian documents this
school counts.

## How to remember it

**Which** one? The one *ša* points at. Every time Akkadian glues
a noun to a noun ("the lord — *which is to say* — of heaven") or
hangs a clause on a noun ("the man *who*…"), this sign does the
pointing. Learn one sign, own the language's hinge.
